title: Efficient photo-ionizing elimination of detrimental electric fields for Rydberg atoms
authors: Zhou-Chen Deng, Hao-Nan Lin, Yu-Cheng Duan, Qi Zhang, Xiang-Can Cheng, Yang Liu, Zhao-Yang Yuan, Jie Li, Peng Liu, Zhan Wu, Chao-Yang Lu, Jun Rui, Jian-Wei Pan
abstract: Rydberg atoms are highly sensitive to external electric fields due to their exaggerated electronic properties. This unique feature lays the foundation for many of their applications in quantum science. However, an uncontrolled stray electric field can be detrimental, severely degrading their quantum control. In this work, we demonstrate a universal scheme that relies on the efficient creation of an in-vacuum plasma source by photo-ionizing laser-cooled atoms to eliminate detrimental electric fields in a Rydberg-atom tweezer array platform, requiring only readily available resources. With this method, we began with a Stark-ionized Rydberg continuum spectrum caused by a large, unknown stray electric field and ultimately recovered stable, coherent excitation of an individual Rydberg state after fully eliminating the field. Our method is directly applicable to existing Rydberg-atom platforms and can also be useful in other experiments sensitive to stray electric fields.
summary: The research addresses the critical challenge of stray electric fields corrupting measurements on highly sensitive Rydberg atoms. The authors introduce and experimentally validate a novel method that uses photo-ionization to generate an in-vacuum plasma capable of neutralizing these detrimental fields. This technique restores spectral coherence, enabling reliable quantum control experiments on trapped Rydberg arrays.
main_problem: Uncontrolled stray electric fields severely degrade quantum control experiments involving highly sensitive Rydberg atoms.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a universal method using in-vacuum plasma generation to efficiently eliminate detrimental stray electric fields, restoring stable and coherent excitation of individual Rydberg states.
method: They employ photo-ionization by laser-cooled atoms to create an in-vacuum plasma source that neutralizes the ambient electric field, which is then verified by monitoring spectroscopic shifts.
model_or_system: The experiment uses Strontium (Sr) Rydberg atoms trapped in an optical tweezer array platform. The system's sensitivity arises from the large dipole moments of highly excited Rydberg states ($n \gg 1$).
key_observables: Rydberg state resonance frequency shifts, Rabi oscillation frequencies, and spectral homogeneity across the atom array.
important_parameters: Stray electric field strength (initially $>10 	ext{ V/cm}$), ionization rates ($\sim 10^3$ ion-electron pairs per ms), and coherence time constants.
main_assumptions: The initial stray fields are attributed to material properties of the vacuum cell, and the plasma generation mechanism is robustly controllable for field neutralization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup (Rydberg laser ionizing atoms in a MOT), show resonance frequency shifts confirming field dependence, and finally display uniform site-resolved spectra after successful field elimination.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the problem of stray fields causing spectral distortion to presenting the novel plasma neutralization protocol. It then validates this by showing recovery of coherent Rabi oscillations and achieving highly homogeneous excitation across the array.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, practical technique for mitigating environmental noise (static/DC electric fields) in advanced Rydberg quantum simulations, directly impacting the feasibility of high-fidelity quantum control experiments.
